takeaways: The machine works, a bit: best model (4h_blend_price-volume_monthly_t24h) made Sharpe 0.84 after taker costs on the untouched holdout (2025-07 -> 2026-10), 1.025 at zero cost, vol 10.75%/yr.
But Jim's own one-line 20 day trend (long the top third of 20 day movers, short the bottom third, smoothed) did better on the same holdout: Sharpe 1.391 after taker costs.

LightGBM found REAL fast signal: holdout Sharpe 1.495 at zero cost when it trades every 4h bar. At taker costs (7 bp/side) the same book is -4.349. The edge is too fast for retail fees. Slowing it down kills the signal.
Costs decide everything. Turnover control (smoothing the score) moved models from deeply negative to positive. 1h bars lost to costs in every model except the 20 day trend, so 4h is the main horizon.
Retraining did NOT help here: from 2023 on, a model trained once on 2020-2022 did as well as monthly retrains. The signals that work (trend, low vol, taker flow) were stable, not fading.
2026 so far is negative (Sharpe -1.92 after costs). The edge is shrinking right now, which is Jim's 'anomalies fade' showing up in real time.
Capacity is small: square-root impact says the edge is half gone near $10M and gone near $38M on these 16 coins.
Fees: 5 and 44 on a 10% vol book leaves investors 3.61%/yr (fund made 15.14%/yr before fees). Renaissance fees need a much bigger edge than this.
